Visit note | 2025-08-20 11:30 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Jannat Ahmed, 50, female. Mrs. Ahmed attends for her first visit complaining of a lower belly ache, going to the toilet frequently, and a burning sensation when passing urine. She mentions these problems began during a hot week with little water intake in Rangpur. Her occupation is a restaurant cook. She has no known comorbidities and denies fever or back pain. On examination: temperature 99.5°F, BP 133/77 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 90 kg. Abdomen is soft with mild suprapubic tenderness. Assessment: Uncomplicated urinary tract infection. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to drink at least two litres of water daily and not to hold urine for long periods. Follow-up in 1 week if symptoms continue.
